title: What Is a Citation in AI Search? A Simple Explanation
description: A citation is when ChatGPT, Perplexity or Google AI names your page as the source of an answer. Here's exactly what counts, and what doesn't.
focusKeyword: what is a citation in AI search
bodyMarkdown:
Quick answer

A citation is when an AI tool like ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google's AI Overviews names your website as the source behind a fact in its answer, usually as a clickable link. It's the AI-era version of ranking on page one, except there's no list of ten links. There's just the one (or few) pages the AI decided to trust.

Key takeaways
  • A citation is a named, attributed source behind a specific fact in an AI answer, usually shown as a link.
  • It's different from just being "mentioned" (more on that in a separate post) and different from ranking in classic Google search.
  • Most AI engines cite only a handful of sources per answer, so the competition for each citation slot is tighter than it looks.
  • Whether you get cited depends on whether the AI's crawler can actually read your page, not just whether a human can.
If you've ever asked ChatGPT or Perplexity a question and seen a little link or footnote next to part of the answer, that's a citation. The AI picked a specific page, decided it supported a specific claim, and told you where that claim came from. ## What actually counts as a citation? Not every time your brand or website comes up in an AI answer is a citation. A citation specifically means: - The AI names a **specific page** (not just "a website" or "some sources say"). - That page is shown as a link, a footnote number, or a clearly labeled source. - The citation is tied to a **specific claim or fact**, not a vague general reference. For example, if Perplexity answers "How long should a Google Play experiment run?" and links to a specific article right next to the answer, that's a citation. If ChatGPT just says "many SEO experts recommend testing for two weeks" with no link at all, that's not a citation, even though it might be loosely based on something it read. ## How is this different from ranking on Google? On Google, you compete for one of ten blue links on a results page, and a person decides which one to click. With an AI citation, the AI engine has already read several pages, picked the best one (or two or three), and shown you the answer directly. There's no list to scroll through. You're either the page it picked, or you're invisible for that specific question. | | Classic Google ranking | AI citation | |---|---|---| | How many spots exist | Usually 10 per page | Often just 1 to 3 per answer | | What the user sees | A list of links to choose from | The answer, plus the source(s) behind it | | What you're optimizing for | Clicks | Being the trusted source, even with no click | This is also the core idea behind AEO vs SEO vs GEO, if you want the fuller picture of how these goals differ. [[chart:0]] > Being cited by name, with no click at all, is still a real result. It means the AI trusted your page enough to put your name next to a fact it's telling someone. ## Why does my page never get cited, even though it ranks on Google? This is the single most common surprise for site owners. Ranking well on Google and getting cited by an AI engine are two different achievements, measured two different ways. A few reasons a page can rank fine on Google but never get cited by AI: 1. **The AI crawler can't actually read the page.** Most AI crawlers (GPTBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot) don't run JavaScript the way Googlebot does. If your content loads in after the page renders, Google sees it and the AI crawler doesn't. 2. **The answer isn't stated clearly enough to quote.** AI engines favor direct, self-contained answers. A page that makes its point across three paragraphs of buildup is harder to extract from than one that states the answer plainly, high up. 3. **robots.txt is quietly blocking the crawler that matters.** Some sites block AI bots without realizing which ones actually gate citations versus which ones are just for training. You can check exactly what each AI crawler sees on your own page with the free LLM Access Check, which fetches your page using the real crawler user agents and shows you, element by element, what got through. ## Does getting cited actually matter for my traffic? It's a fair question, since a citation often doesn't come with a click. The honest answer: it matters for visibility and trust, even without the click. Being the named source in an AI answer puts your brand in front of someone at the exact moment they're deciding something, which is a form of reach that doesn't show up in your analytics but is very real. For a deeper breakdown of what to actually do about it, the Full AEO & GEO Audit scores a page against the specific checks that affect citation likelihood, not just classic SEO. ## How do I actually get cited more often? There's no single trick, but the underlying pattern is consistent: write a clear, direct answer near the top, back it with real data or a named source where you can, structure the page so a machine can easily tell what the page is about, and make sure the AI crawlers that matter can actually fetch your page. The full checklist is laid out on the AEO & GEO checklist page if you want the complete list in one place.

faqs.q: Is a citation the same thing as a backlink?
faqs.a: No. A backlink is a link from someone else's page to yours, built over time for SEO. A citation is an AI engine naming your page as the source of a specific fact, decided fresh for each individual question someone asks.

faqs.q: Can I see if ChatGPT or Perplexity has ever cited my page?
faqs.a: There's no public dashboard for this yet, the way Google Search Console shows your rankings. The practical approach is to ask the AI engines directly about topics you cover and see what gets cited, or run a structural check like the free LLM Access Check to see whether your page is even readable to their crawlers in the first place.

faqs.q: Do I need a lot of traffic or domain authority to get cited?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. AI engines are looking for a clear, trustworthy, extractable answer to the specific question being asked, not overall site authority the way Google's ranking has traditionally leaned. A smaller, well-structured page can get cited over a bigger, vaguer one.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a citation and just being mentioned?
faqs.a: A citation names a specific page as the source of a specific claim, usually with a link. A mention is when your brand or name comes up without that formal source attribution. See the companion post on mentions for the full comparison.

faqs.q: Does the same page get cited by every AI engine?
faqs.a: No, and this surprises a lot of people. ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews often cite different sources for the same question, because each one crawls, indexes and judges trust slightly differently.

faqs.q: Is a citation more valuable than a Google ranking?
faqs.a: They're valuable for different things. A Google ranking still drives clicks. A citation builds visibility and trust at the moment of an AI answer, often with no click, so treat them as two separate goals rather than one replacing the other.
